findings.title: LEADING_IDENTITY deviation claims a parameterisation escape hatch that does not exist
locations: workflow/payload/policy.md:72-79 — rendered RULE.DOC.LEADING_IDENTITY: "For this package the identity leads with the physical meaning — what the operation does to its object, before how it is computed"

workflow/payload/policy.md:732 — deviations.md: "this package computes no physical quantity, so its docstrings lead with what the operation does, which the rubric's own parameterisation already admits"
src/CLI/Sync.jl:78-81 — `const IDENTITY_TEXT = Dict("physical-meaning" => "the physical meaning — ...", "estimand" => "the estimand — ...")`
src/CLI/Init.jl:150 — `"rubric" => Dict("leading_identity" => "physical-meaning")` seeded unconditionally for every new consumer
findings.description: The deviations ledger excuses GBGCodingTools from RULE.DOC.LEADING_IDENTITY on the ground that the rubric's own per-package parameterisation 'already admits' non-physical wording ('leads with what the operation does') for a package that computes no physical quantity. But Sync.jl's IDENTITY_TEXT dictionary has exactly two values, 'physical-meaning' and 'estimand', and both keep the literal phrase 'the physical meaning'; Init.jl seeds every consumer, including this one, with 'physical-meaning'. There is no config value that renders as 'what the operation does' without that phrase, and the rule as actually rendered in this same policy.md still reads 'the identity leads with the physical meaning' — directly contradicting the deviation's own premise. Contrast with the vector-notation parameter, which has a genuine "none" => "not used (the package has no vector quantities)" escape hatch (Sync.jl:85); LEADING_IDENTITY has no equivalent third value.
findings.resolution_hint: Add a third `rubric.leading_identity` value (e.g. "operational") whose IDENTITY_TEXT drops the 'physical meaning' phrase, or correct the deviation's wording so it stops claiming the parameterisation already admits this and instead states plainly that this package's docstrings keep the physical-meaning template though it does not compute physical quantities.
findings.contradicts: workflow/payload/policy.md:732 (deviations.md's own LEADING_IDENTITY entry) vs. workflow/payload/policy.md:72-79 (the rule it is describing) and src/CLI/Sync.jl:78-81

findings.title: FULL_INLINE's unconditional 'one bullet per work' contradicts BLOCK_LIST's lone-citation form
locations: workflow/payload/policy.md:439-443 — RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE: "carries the full reference in a `# References` section ... one bullet per work"
workflow/payload/policy.md:453-455 — RULE.CIT.BLOCK_LIST: "a lone citation stays inline as `Reference: …`"
src/Scans/doi_crosscheck.jl:10 — "A one-line `Reference: …` stays legal, being the lone-citation form of RULE.CIT.BLOCK_LIST."
findings.description: RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE states the docstring's own `# References` section is always 'one bullet per work' with no exception for a single reference. RULE.CIT.BLOCK_LIST and the actual scan (SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK, which explicitly treats a bare `Reference:` line as legal even under a docstring's `# References` heading) both establish that a single reference takes the unbulleted inline 'Reference: …' form instead. A reader following FULL_INLINE's own sentence literally would bullet even a single-reference docstring, which the implemented and cross-referenced rule forbids.
findings.resolution_hint: Add FULL_INLINE's single-reference exception (or an explicit cross-reference to BLOCK_LIST, mirroring how HOME_ORDER's own text resolves its three-way 'end of docstring' overlap) so the two rules state one consistent format.

findings.title: STEER and RETURNS are mechanically checkable rules with no scan implementing them
locations: workflow/payload/policy.md:115-120 — RULE.DOC.STEER: the exact verbatim in-place steer sentence
workflow/payload/policy.md:303-307 — RULE.DOC.RETURNS: "arrow and sentence never both appear"
src/Scans/ (41 files) — `grep -rl steer src/Scans/` and `grep -rl RETURNS src/Scans/` both return nothing
src/Scans/ai_banner.jl:1-27 — the structurally identical verbatim-sentence rule RULE.DOC.AI_BANNER DOES have SCAN.AI_BANNER, built on a shared `AI_BANNER` text constant
findings.description: STEER requires an exact, verbatim sentence naming the destination argument — exactly the shape AI_BANNER's rule takes, and AI_BANNER has its own scan (SCAN.AI_BANNER) comparing page text against a shared constant. RETURNS forbids an arrow and a 'Returns' sentence from co-occurring, a plain syntactic check. Neither rule has an entry among the 41 files in src/Scans/, nor any reference in src/CLI/Doctor.jl. This lane's ground-truth snapshot did not include policy/RULES.toml, catalog/scans.toml or test/, so it is possible RULES.toml legitimately records `panel` for one or both with a stated reason — but nothing visible in src/, ext/, docs/ or instruments/*/schema.json backs that, and per RULE.TEST.RULE_WITH_CHECK's own warning an unchecked-but-checkable rule's mere presence 'reads as compliance.'
findings.resolution_hint: Confirm and record an explicit `panel` check (with reason) for STEER and RETURNS in RULES.toml if that is the intended tier, or add scans analogous to SCAN.AI_BANNER.
